title: Basie's telegram and joining his band in 1942
summary: Basie's booker wired him to join in New Jersey; he filled in for the ill Jo Jones for about six weeks without rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Any way, it must have been about this time that you got the call from Basie, wasn't it, to go to New Jersey?
Later.
Later? I thought it was the late forties.
It was later,yeah.
What year did you go east to join Basie's band?
That was in about '32.
No, no, no, it had to be much later than that.
No, wait a minute.
Wait a minute. Yeah, that was in '42.
Well, see, we're out of sequence now.
In other words we're up to the late forties, out on highway 40,
but you didn't mention going with Basie in '42. Where were you playing when you left to go with Basie and with whom were you playing?
I don't think I was working any place when Basie called.
What did you do get a telegram or a letter.
Yeah, yeah.
You got a telegram.
Yeah. He wired me. Macey O'Burch wired me, Basie's booker.
Oh, yeah.
His manager.
Who was his manager.
Macey O'Burch.
Macey O'Burch?
Yeah, he was booking Basie then.

Uh-huh. And he wired you to join the band in New Jersey. We're going to come back to that. All right, and how long were you with Basie?
About six weeks.
Six weeks.
Right.
And then you came back to Kansas City.
Right.
What did Jo' Jones rejoin the band?
Yes. Jo -- when he sent for me, Jo were ill at the time, you know, and he sent for me.
And you filled in for Jo.
And I -- without any rehearsal or anything.
